newsitem.title: USA: LILCO says no impact from NY substation fire.
newsitem.headline: LILCO says no impact from NY substation fire.

text.p: Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) said a fire this weekend at a substation on the Queens, Nassau Counties border was not affecting power transmissions.
The distribution substation in Valley Stream, Long Island, was shut while the blaze is being investigated, a LILCO spokeswoman said.
The facility reduces voltage of power from 33 kilovolt (KV) transmission lines from the region's power plants to 4 KV distribution lines that run to homes and small businesses.
"We think it's in the switchgear, but we're not sure. It could take weeks (to learn the cause) because the damage was so extensive," said a LILCO spokeswoman.

She said the fire broke out Saturday, knocking out power to more than 9,000 LILCO customers. About 1,300 customers experienced outages up to 70 minutes, while the rest lost power for just under half an hour.
LILCO has been re-routed power to those consumers through other circuits, she added.
